chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from one of our companions, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ṣandal al-Khayyāṭ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام concerning His, the Exalted's, saying:
“This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without reckoning.”

He عليه السلام said: “He gave Sulaymān a magnificent kingdom. Then this verse came to apply regarding the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, so he had the authority to give whatever he wished to whomever he wished, and to withhold from whomever he wished. And Allah gave him better than what He gave Sulaymān, due to His saying:”
“Whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you from, refrain.”

key_terms.بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ: without reckoning or accountability; indicating unrestricted divine grant
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, to whom the verse is applied in the hadith
key_terms.عَطَاؤُنَا: Our gift; the divine bestowal mentioned in the verse
key_terms.مَا آتَاكُمُ: whatever he gives you; a command to accept the Messenger’s grant
key_terms.مُلْكًا: kingdom or sovereignty; the great dominion given to Sulaymān عليه السلام
key_terms.نَهَاكُمْ: he forbade you; indicating the Messenger’s binding prohibition
key_terms.يُمْنَعَ: to withhold; part of the described authority to grant or prevent

ai.seo_question: How does Qur'an 38:39 relate to the authority of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: The hadith explains that the divine grant mentioned for Sulaymān عليه السلام also has an application to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, indicating his God-given authority to give and withhold by divine sanction. It further affirms that Allah granted the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله a rank greater than that granted to Sulaymān عليه السلام, as shown by the command to accept whatever the Messenger brings and refrain from whatever he forbids.
